key_insight: DSWorld learns to predict the next state of a data science workflow, letting autonomous agents avoid many expensive trial-and-error executions.
engineering_relevance: It can speed up training and search for data science agents by routing cheap steps through structured prediction and reserving real execution for costly operations.
method: Builds a structured representation of workflow state and candidate operations
Uses cost-aware routing to choose between lightweight execution and an LLM-based simulator
Trains with an 8K transition trajectory dataset and Reflective World Model Optimization
evidence_signal: The abstract reports about 14× faster RL-based agent training, 3–6× faster search-based inference, and 35.6% better transition prediction than the strongest LLM baseline.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate transition prediction, so errors in simulated state updates or routing decisions could still propagate through agent training and inference.
paper_title: DSWorld: A Data Science World Model for Efficient Autonomous Agents
